text.p: The following are the reports carried by Estonia's newspapers on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- The Coalition Party and the rural union has won enough support to continue as a minority government. The opposition has agreed to support the government on vital issues. But right-wing parties have refused to participate in cabinet unless the Coalition Party undergoes a major reform.

- Foreign Minister Toomas Hendrik Ilves said at a meeting in the European Commission office in Bonn that the EU should proceed from the results of reforms in determining new members rather than from geo-political considerations.
- Parliament approved a law on refugees and is expected to ratify the U.N. convention today. This should help to establish visa-free travel between Estonia and the Nordic and Schengen countries.
- Swedish firm Ragn & Sells plans a waste dumping ground in southern Estonia, which would meet European requirements.
- Former Bank of Estonia president Siim Kallas doubts whether he signed a document releasing $10 million from a Swiss bank for a failed transaction.
- An important international conference "Baltic security: Considerations before the NATO summit" will open in Tallinn.

- The Moderate Party faction wants to establish unified requirements on broadcasting electoral campaigns for all radio and TV channels and to ban journalist candidates from the media for the duration of the campaign.
- An interview with Fatherland and Moderate MPs concerning the reasons for refusing to join the government.
- New Russian customs regulations have stopped the export of Estonian alcohol. Distilleries may close down because of excess production.
- The government approved the statute and founding documents of the Tiger's Leap foundation, meant for the computerisation of Estonian schools.
